vis.text:
Two looks to accept or reject before any more screens are drawn

1 · Observatory. Dark night-sky ground, the board as a lit plate, hairline instrument panels, monospace labels. The field is light in space: White's pull glows like starlight, Black's like a violet nebula. Manrope + IBM Plex Mono.

2 · Mission. Bright, precise, one electric-blue accent, like a modern spaceflight company. The field is a scientific plate: solid dots for White's pull, rings for Black's, sized by strength. Geist + Geist Mono.

Both: the board alone is the share image. All field values, king pulls and commentary are real (gen-004 engine, this position).

alt.text:
Two different directions to compare with rows 1-3

A · The board is the universe. One large centred board, no side panel. Each king's readout sits on the board edge next to that king. Everything else is a thin top line and a bottom dock; moves open in a drawer.

B · The universe narrates. The board plus a running commentary that says in plain words what the field did on each move. People learn the idea by playing, not by reading cards.

Both use a colour-free field: White's pull lights squares up, Black's pull shades them, like light and shadow. Works without colour vision and matches the piece colours.

Every commentary line is a real fact about that position from the engine's breakdown (which squares a piece reaches, where it's blocked).

legend.text:
How to read these wireframes

Low fidelity: layout, content and states only. Colours, fonts and the exact look come in stage D.

The square tints are the real field computed by the gen-004 engine for each position: blue = White pulls harder there, orange = Black does, stronger tint = bigger difference. The hue pair is a placeholder.

Pieces are drawn as lettered discs (K Q R B N P; white discs = White).

Every number shown is real (from the engine or a committed result) or a [PLACEHOLDER] that the game fills in.

n5.text: State 5 has no event: the readout bar just fills. No percentage, no red zone, no "torn apart" moment (decision log 2026-10-25).

n7.text: Moments are computed from the game: where Kepler's score turned, the biggest capture swing, the biggest jump in pull on a king. Each opens that position.

land.text:
How the landing page works

The first screen is Play at rest: a headline beside the real, playable board. Pressing Play White or Play Black turns the page into the Play screen in place, with no new page to load. Nobody has to get through a landing page to play.

Below it, three short sections, one idea and one real visual each: the one law, the self-found piece values (real curves from both equal-start runs), and the Law Ledger with the rejected laws. The ladder and the v0 story are one link each, into Lab. Then open source. Shared-game and universe links skip this page and open the board directly.

The small planet-and-ring mark is the only space ornament: logo, section ends, footer.
